title: Instant Pot French-Style Coq au Vin with Mushrooms
dek: Chicken thighs braise in a glossy red-wine sauce with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions, delivering weekend character on a family-night timeline.
image_alt: Chicken pieces and mushrooms in a dark red-wine sauce served in a wide white bowl
ingredients: 4 oz thick-cut bacon, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
8 oz frozen pearl onions, thawed and patted dry
Mashed potatoes or crusty bread, optional for serving

instructions.name: Season and brown the chicken
instructions.text: Pat chicken very dry and season with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Select Sauté High on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Cook bacon until crisp, 5 to 6 minutes, then transfer it to a plate. Brown chicken skin-side down in two batches, 5 minutes per batch, using a little oil only if the pot is dry. Transfer chicken to a clean plate.

instructions.name: Brown the vegetables
instructions.text: Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat. Add mushrooms and pearl onions and cook 5 minutes until spotted brown. Transfer them to the bacon plate so they keep their shape during the pressure cycle.

instructions.name: Build a clean thin base
instructions.text: Add carrot and garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in tomato paste for 30 seconds, then pour in wine. Scrape every browned bit from the heating plate and simmer 3 minutes. Add 1 cup broth, thyme, bay leaf and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt; scrape once more until the base is completely smooth.

instructions.name: Layer and pressure-cook
instructions.text: Set the chicken in the thin liquid, skin-side up, without stirring tomato solids underneath it. Lock the lid and cook on High Pressure for 10 minutes; allow about 12 minutes to reach pressure.

instructions.name: Release in two stages
instructions.text: Let pressure release naturally for 10 minutes. Then vent the remainder in short controlled pulses, keeping hands and face away from steam. Open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Verify chicken and finish vegetables
instructions.text: Check the thickest part of several thighs without touching bone; each must reach 165°F. Transfer chicken to a clean platter. Discard the bay leaf, stir mushrooms, onions and bacon into the pot, and simmer on Sauté Normal for 5 to 7 minutes until the onions are tender.

instructions.name: Thicken after pressure
instructions.text: Mash butter and flour into a smooth paste. Whisk it into the simmering sauce a teaspoon at a time, adding the remaining 1/2 cup broth as needed, and cook 2 minutes until glossy. Return chicken just long enough to coat and heat through.

instructions.name: Serve mild-first
instructions.text: Taste for salt, scatter with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes or bread. Offer cracked pepper or chile flakes at the table rather than making the shared braise hot.

why_it_works: Wine is reduced before pressure and joined by a full cup of thin broth over a completely deglazed base, lowering burn-warning risk.
Mushrooms and pearl onions brown first but finish after pressure, so the sauce gains savory depth without turning the vegetables to mush.
The flour-butter thickener goes in only after pressure; the cook phase stays fluid enough to circulate and seal correctly.
swaps: Use skinless bone-in thighs and add 1 tablespoon oil for browning; keep the pressure time and 165°F safety check.
Replace wine with 3/4 cup additional chicken broth plus 2 teaspoons red-wine vinegar added after pressure; the sauce will be lighter but balanced.
For a pork-free version, omit bacon and brown the chicken and mushrooms in 2 tablespoons olive oil.
storage: Cool chicken and sauce in shallow containers within 2 hours and refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently to 165°F, thinning the sauce with broth. Freeze up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating.
notes: Total time includes batch browning, wine reduction, about 12 minutes to pressurize, the 10-minute cook, a 10-minute natural release and post-pressure sauce finishing.
Follow the exact model manual for locking, minimum liquid and venting. Do not exceed the two-thirds line or double this recipe in a 6-quart cooker.
Never force the lid. If the valve sputters during the controlled release, close it, wait 2 minutes and resume in shorter pulses.
Chicken is safe only when multiple thighs register 165°F at their thickest points; return any under-temperature pieces for additional cooking.

faqs.q: Does all the alcohol cook out?
faqs.a: No method guarantees zero alcohol. The wine simmers before pressure and cooks again in the sauce, but use the broth-and-vinegar swap when complete avoidance matters.

faqs.q: Why is the sauce thickened after pressure cooking?
faqs.a: Flour and other starches can settle on the heating plate and trigger a burn warning. Keeping the pressure liquid thin is safer and gives better control over the final consistency.

faqs.q: Can I make coq au vin ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Chill it promptly, then lift off any firm surface fat and reheat gently to 165°F. The flavor deepens overnight and the sauce can be loosened with broth.

title: Instant Pot Vegan Corn & Potato Chowder with Chives
dek: Sweet corn and Yukon Gold potatoes turn naturally creamy in a dairy-free chowder finished with oat milk, chives and bright lemon.
image_alt: Creamy golden corn chowder with visible corn kernels, diced vegetables and chopped chives in a white bowl
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
5 cups corn kernels, fresh or frozen, divided
Black pepper and hot sauce, optional for serving

instructions.name: Soften the aromatics
instructions.text: Select Sauté Normal on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Heat oil, then cook onion, carrots and celery with 1/2 teaspoon salt for 5 minutes. Add garlic, smoked paprika and thyme and stir for 30 seconds.

instructions.name: Deglaze completely
instructions.text: Pour in 1 cup broth and scrape until the heating plate is perfectly smooth. Cancel Sauté. Add remaining 3 cups broth, potatoes and 4 cups corn; stir only to distribute in the thin liquid.

instructions.name: Pressure-cook
instructions.text: Lock the lid and cook on High Pressure for 5 minutes; allow about 12 minutes to reach pressure. Keep the pot below the two-thirds line and do not reduce the four cups of thin broth.

instructions.name: Use a controlled quick release
instructions.text: Wait 5 minutes after the cycle, then vent in short controlled pulses. If starchy steam sputters, close the valve, wait 2 minutes and continue more slowly. Open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Blend for natural body
instructions.text: Scoop 3 cups soup into a heat-safe blender, vent the lid and blend in small pulses, or use an immersion blender directly in the pot for 8 to 10 short pulses. Leave plenty of potato and corn intact.

instructions.name: Finish without dairy
instructions.text: Select Sauté Low. Stir in oat milk, nutritional yeast, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and the reserved 1 cup corn. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the fresh corn is tender and the chowder reaches 165°F; do not pressure-cook the oat milk.

instructions.name: Brighten and serve mild-first
instructions.text: Turn off the cooker, stir in lemon juice and half the chives, and adjust salt. Ladle into bowls and top with remaining chives. Put black pepper and hot sauce on the table.

why_it_works: Four cups of thin broth cover a fully deglazed base; oat milk and nutritional yeast stay out until after pressure to reduce scorching and separation.
Blending only part of the potatoes and corn creates chowder body without flour, cashews or a heavy cream finish.
Reserved corn cooks during the final simmer, adding the distinct kernels and fresh sweetness visible in the finished bowl.
swaps: Use unsweetened soy milk instead of oat milk for more protein; verify it is plain and unflavored.
Substitute red potatoes for Yukon Golds, keeping the cubes 3/4 inch so they cook on the same schedule.
For a non-vegan finish, use whole milk and replace nutritional yeast with 1/2 cup shredded mild cheddar, added off heat.
storage: Cool in shallow containers within 2 hours and refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat to 165°F over low heat, stirring and adding broth as needed. Freeze up to 2 months; the potatoes soften slightly after thawing.
notes: Total time includes vegetable prep, sautéing, about 12 minutes to pressurize, the 5-minute cycle, a 5-minute rest, controlled venting, blending and finishing.
Follow the manual for your exact model. Keep the cooker at or below the two-thirds line and never cover or touch the steam-release mechanism.
Hot purée expands. If using a countertop blender, work in small batches, remove the center cap and cover the opening loosely with a folded towel.
This recipe is written for a 6-quart cooker; do not double it in that size.

faqs.a: Yes. Drain it well and use the same five-cup volume, but expect slightly less fresh sweetness and a softer kernel texture.

faqs.q: Why did my chowder trigger a burn warning?
faqs.a: Common causes are browned bits left on the base, too little thin broth or dairy added before pressure. Scrape the plate completely clean and reserve oat milk for the final simmer.

faqs.q: How can I make it thicker without flour?
faqs.a: Blend one additional cup of the cooked soup, then simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes. The potato starch and puréed corn thicken it naturally.

title: Spanish Tortilla Española with Potato & Onion
dek: Slow-softened potato and onion set inside a golden egg round that slices cleanly for brunch, tapas or a packable room-temperature lunch.
image_alt: Cut wedge of Spanish tortilla showing distinct layers of tender potato bound with golden egg
ingredients: 1 3/4 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/8 inch thick
Roasted red peppers or a simple green salad, optional for serving

instructions.name: Slice evenly
instructions.text: Slice potatoes into uniform 1/8-inch rounds and onion into thin half-moons. A mandoline is efficient, but always use its hand guard and stop before the piece becomes too small to hold safely.

instructions.name: Confit potato and onion
instructions.text: Combine olive oil, potatoes, onion and 1 teaspoon salt in a 10-inch nonstick skillet. Cook over medium-low heat for 18 to 22 minutes, turning gently every few minutes, until potatoes are tender but not browned or falling apart.

instructions.name: Drain and rest
instructions.text: Set a heatproof colander over a bowl and drain the potato mixture for 5 minutes, reserving the oil. The oil can be cooled and refrigerated for another savory use.

instructions.name: Combine with eggs
instructions.text: Whisk eggs with remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper in a large bowl. Fold in warm potatoes and onion without breaking the slices, then rest 10 minutes so the egg settles between the layers.

instructions.name: Set the first side
instructions.text: Wipe the skillet, add 1 tablespoon reserved oil and heat over medium. Pour in the mixture, level the top and cook 4 to 5 minutes. Run a flexible spatula around the edge; the underside should be golden while the top remains loose.

instructions.name: Flip safely
instructions.text: Slide the skillet off heat. Place a flat plate wider than the skillet over it, hold both firmly with dry oven mitts and invert in one decisive motion. Slide the tortilla back into the skillet with 1 teaspoon more oil.

instructions.name: Finish and verify
instructions.text: Cook over medium-low heat 3 to 5 minutes until golden and the center reaches 160°F. For a firm, sliceable tortilla, continue to 165°F. Rest on a board for 10 minutes before cutting into six wedges.

instructions.name: Serve
instructions.text: Sprinkle with parsley if using. Serve warm or at room temperature with peppers or salad; do not leave the egg dish at room temperature longer than 2 hours.

why_it_works: Gentle oil-poaching cooks every potato slice through without building a hard crust, creating the layered interior shown in the photograph.
A 10-minute rest lets warm potatoes absorb seasoned egg so the tortilla binds cleanly instead of separating when flipped.
An instant-read thermometer removes the guesswork from the thick center while the short final rest firms each wedge.
swaps: Use waxy red potatoes, peeled or unpeeled, and keep the slices the same thickness.
Omit onion for a simpler potato tortilla; add 1/4 teaspoon extra salt to the egg mixture.
Use a well-seasoned 10-inch carbon-steel skillet if you are confident eggs release from it; nonstick is the most forgiving choice.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate tightly covered for up to 3 days. Serve chilled or reheat wedges in a 300°F oven until 165°F. Freezing is not recommended because potato slices become watery.
notes: Total time includes a 10-minute egg-and-potato rest and a 10-minute rest after cooking.
The flip involves hot oil and a heavy skillet. Use a flat plate with no raised rim, dry mitts and a clear counter; slide the tortilla rather than attempting a second airborne flip.
Egg dishes should reach 160°F. Refrigerate promptly and avoid extended room-temperature service.
Strain, cool and refrigerate the reserved olive oil; use within one week for sautéing vegetables or another tortilla.

faqs.q: Should Spanish tortilla be runny in the center?
faqs.a: Some traditional versions are soft-set, but this family recipe reaches at least 160°F for safe egg doneness and clean, packable slices.

faqs.q: Can I bake it instead of flipping?
faqs.a: After the first side sets, transfer the oven-safe skillet to a 375°F oven for 7 to 10 minutes. The top will be paler and the texture slightly firmer.

faqs.q: Is all the olive oil absorbed?
faqs.a: No. Most drains away after the potato and onion soften. The quantity provides even, gentle cooking, and the cooled strained oil can be reused for savory cooking.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Shawarma Stuffed Pitas
dek: Warm-spiced roasted chicken, creamy garlic yogurt and quick-pickled carrots tuck into toasted pitas for a build-your-own dinner that travels well.
image_alt: Chopped chicken shawarma and creamy sauce stuffed between two toasted pita rounds with pickled vegetables
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
2 large carrots, cut into thin sticks
Hot sauce or sliced chiles, optional for serving

instructions.name: Marinate the chicken
instructions.text: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, half the garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, 1 teaspoon salt and pepper. Coat chicken and refrigerate 20 minutes while the oven heats to 450°F with a rimmed sheet pan inside.

instructions.name: Quick-pickle the carrots
instructions.text: Stir vinegar, sugar and 1/4 teaspoon salt until dissolved. Add carrot sticks, toss and let stand at least 20 minutes. Drain before serving.

instructions.name: Mix the garlic yogurt
instructions.text: Stir yogurt, tahini, lemon zest, remaining garlic and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Refrigerate until serving so the sauce stays cold and thick.

instructions.name: Roast on a hot pan
instructions.text: Carefully arrange chicken in one layer on the preheated sheet pan. Roast 18 to 22 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and every thigh reaches 165°F at its thickest point.

instructions.name: Rest and chop
instructions.text: Move chicken to a clean board and rest 5 minutes. Chop across the grain into small pieces. For crisper edges, spread the pieces back on the pan and broil 1 to 2 minutes, watching continuously.

instructions.name: Warm the pitas
instructions.text: Wrap pitas in foil and warm in the turned-off oven for 5 minutes, or toast them briefly in a dry skillet. Keep covered so they remain flexible.

instructions.name: Build the stuffed pitas
instructions.text: Split each pita and spread with garlic yogurt. Fill with chopped chicken, romaine and drained pickled carrots. Serve immediately with hot sauce or sliced chiles at the table.

why_it_works: A preheated sheet pan starts browning immediately, giving marinated thighs dark edges without a vertical rotisserie.
Thighs stay juicy at 165°F, and a brief rest keeps their juices in the meat before it is chopped for the pita filling.
Cool yogurt and sharp quick pickles balance the warm spices while keeping the shared chicken mild enough for a family table.
swaps: Use 2 pounds chicken breast cutlets and begin checking at 14 minutes; remove each piece as soon as it reaches 165°F.
Replace Greek yogurt with an unsweetened nondairy yogurt and use a thick brand so it does not run out of the pita.
Substitute thinly sliced cucumber for romaine, but assemble only at serving so the bread stays firm.
storage: Refrigerate chicken, sauce, pickles and lettuce in separate containers for up to 4 days. Reheat chicken to 165°F and warm pitas separately. Freeze cooked chicken up to 2 months; do not freeze the yogurt sauce or lettuce.
notes: Total time includes a 20-minute marinade that overlaps with oven heating and pickle preparation, plus the 5-minute chicken rest.
Discard marinade that contacted raw chicken and use a clean board and utensils after cooking.
Check the thickest parts of multiple thighs for 165°F; pan color alone is not a doneness test.
For packed lunches, keep components chilled and assemble shortly before eating.

faqs.q: Can I marinate the chicken overnight?
faqs.a: Yes, but limit the lemon marinade to about 12 hours so the surface texture does not become mealy. Keep it covered and refrigerated.

faqs.q: Why is my chicken pale instead of browned?
faqs.a: The pan may not have preheated, or the pieces may be crowded. Use one large hot pan, leave space between thighs and use the short broil only after safe doneness is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can I make bowls instead of pitas?
faqs.a: Yes. Serve the same chicken, yogurt and pickles over rice or chopped romaine. That changes the format without changing the cooking method.

title: Argentine Alfajores de Maicena with Dulce de Leche
dek: Tender lemon-vanilla cornstarch cookies sandwich thick dulce de leche, with coconut around the edges for the classic bakery finish.
image_alt: Pale round alfajores sandwich cookies filled with dulce de leche and rolled in finely shredded coconut
ingredients: 1 to 2 tbsp whole milk, only if needed
1 1/4 cups thick pastry-style dulce de leche

instructions.name: Combine the dry ingredients
instructions.text: Whisk cornstarch, flour, baking powder and salt thoroughly. Line two sheet pans with parchment and heat the oven to 350°F.

instructions.name: Cream gently
instructions.text: Beat butter and sugar on medium speed for 2 minutes until smooth and slightly lighter, not dramatically fluffy. Beat in yolks one at a time, then vanilla and lemon zest.

instructions.name: Make a tender dough
instructions.text: Mix in dry ingredients on low just until clumps form. Press together by hand. If dry crumbs will not hold, add milk 1 teaspoon at a time; avoid overmixing once the flour is hydrated.

instructions.name: Chill and roll
instructions.text: Flatten dough into a disk, wrap and chill 30 minutes. Roll between parchment sheets to 1/4 inch thick. Cut 28 rounds with a 2 1/2-inch cutter and place 1 inch apart on the pans.

instructions.name: Bake pale and tender
instructions.text: Bake one pan at a time for 10 to 12 minutes, rotating once, until tops are dry and bottoms only barely golden. Do not brown the tops. Cool 5 minutes on the pan, then completely on a rack.

instructions.name: Fill the sandwiches
instructions.text: Pipe or spoon about 1 1/2 tablespoons dulce de leche onto the flat side of 14 cookies. Top with the remaining rounds and press gently until filling reaches the edge.

instructions.name: Coat and settle
instructions.text: Roll each exposed filling edge in coconut. Rest assembled alfajores in a covered container for at least 1 hour so the cookie and filling settle into a neat, tender sandwich.

why_it_works: A cornstarch-forward dough bakes into the delicate, pale crumb that distinguishes alfajores de maicena from ordinary shortbread sandwiches.
Chilling and rolling between parchment limits added flour, so the rounds keep their shape without becoming dry.
Thick pastry-style dulce de leche holds a generous edge that gives the coconut something to grip, matching the finished cookies in the photograph.
swaps: Use finely shredded sweetened coconut if that is what is available; the finished cookie will be sweeter.
Orange zest can replace lemon zest for a warmer citrus note.
Do not replace cornstarch cup-for-cup with flour; that would create a different, firmer cookie and remove the defining texture.
storage: Store assembled alfajores airtight at cool room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days; bring to room temperature before serving. Freeze unfilled cookies up to 2 months, then thaw and fill.
notes: Total time includes 30 minutes chilling, baking in batches, cooling enough to fill and a 1-hour covered settling period; much of that time is hands-off.
Use commercial or safely prepared dulce de leche. Do not boil an unopened can, which can rupture.
Weigh cornstarch and flour when possible; compacted cups can make these delicate cookies chalky.
Because the dough contains egg yolks, avoid tasting it raw and wash tools and surfaces after handling.

faqs.a: The dough may have too much flour or too little moisture. Weigh the dry ingredients, mix only until combined and add milk by the teaspoon only until the dough holds together.

faqs.q: Can I use caramel sauce instead of dulce de leche?
faqs.a: Pourable caramel is too loose. Use a thick pastry-style dulce de leche that holds a mound and will not run from the sandwich.

faqs.q: Why should the cookies stay pale?
faqs.a: Browning dries the cornstarch-heavy dough and changes its delicate texture. Look for set, matte tops and only the faintest color underneath.
